scenes.headline: How JEPA-Anything splits a prediction into factors
scenes.sub: One training recipe for cells, patients, fluids, robots and weather.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Ladoo! This paper offers one recipe for world models across very different data. Here is how its predictor works.

scenes.text: Split the latent target into orthogonal blocks, predict each block with its own small head, then stitch the blocks back into one state.
scenes.say: The idea: split the latent target into orthogonal blocks, give each its own small predictor, and stitch them back into one state.

steps.say: An online encoder reads the context: visible patches, a patient's history, or a state plus an action.
A slow moving average of that encoder reads the target. It gets no gradient, so it cannot chase the predictor.
Learned projectors cut the target into four blocks, pushed to be orthogonal so no two blocks repeat a direction.
Each block gets its own small head, trained to match it. Variance floors keep every coordinate alive.
A pseudoinverse stitches the four predictions into one full state, for a decoder, a planner, or the next rollout step.
In the paper's figure, a standard JEPA pours everything into one monolithic target embedding.
JEPA-Anything gives each factor its own predictor and recombines them into a complete latent world state.

left.title: Changes per domain
left.say: Per domain, almost everything changes: the adapter, the encoder, the readout and the weights.

right.title: Shared across all
right.say: What is shared is the recipe: the moving average target, the factor heads, and the pseudoinverse.

scenes.title: Gain over a matched JEPA
scenes.note: Relative error reduction, paper's ten-task benchmark
scenes.say: Against the same model with one head, error drops by about forty percent on a fluid equation, ten on weather, and almost nothing on pixel control.

scenes.text: JEPA-Anything is one portable change to a JEPA's predictor, not one network for every world.
scenes.say: The takeaway: a cheap, portable change to any JEPA's predictor. One recipe, not one network for every world.

recap: Split the latent target into orthogonal blocks
scenes.say: To recap: split the target into orthogonal blocks, one small head per block, and a pseudoinverse to rebuild the state.
